text: The two helpers are published as versioned platform library artefacts pinned by the service template, together with the rest of the shared library baseline of RWB-PLT-NF02-APP.
why: Architecture v5 slide 20 puts every service on the service template and the shared libraries, and N009 is a platform key with no service of its own, so the helper must reach the 19 services through one pinned set; no source names the package, the registry or the version label of that set.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (every service from the service template and the shared libraries); Change Register v1 N009 row; RWB-PLT-NF02-APP sections 3 and 13 (one baseline release, one pin in the template)
confirm: Platform team at the wave 0 baseline review
impact: Names the distribution of the helper and the pin only; no rule, no business value and no service path changes

text: The idempotency store is the idempotency_key table of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON applied in each service's own schema, so the helper creates no table of its own.
why: The Ownership Map keeps idempotency_key with PLT as a library object created in every service schema, and Architecture v5 slide 29 forbids a cross-schema write; the implementation cannot place the stored response without that ruling.
read: Ownership Map v1 idempotency_key row (owner PLT, library object created in every service schema); RWB-PLT-TE006-CON section 12.7 (the DDL template applied by each service's own Flyway sequence); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20 and 29
confirm: ACE DBA and platform team at the wave 0 design gate
impact: The stored response is written in the calling service's own schema; the helper adds no table, no column and no schema

text: The error map is a data file shipped with the library, keyed by message code, holding the HTTP status and the problem type, and never a literal in service code.
why: Architecture v5 slide 11 fixes RFC 9457 problem details but names no store of the mapping from a message code to a status and a type, while the message codes belong to the message catalogue; a shipped data file is the only read that keeps a new code out of nineteen code bases.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (RFC 9457 problem details on every error) and slide 20 (template and shared libraries); Ownership Map v1; RWB-PLT-N009-CON section 13 (error map columns)
confirm: Message-catalogue owner and platform team at the contract freeze
impact: The map is data; a new message code is a map row and a library release, not a code change in a service

text: The header is Idempotency-Key, case-insensitive, and a stored response is scoped to the service, the operation and the key; the expiry window is a chart value and its default is not specified — the working read is the platform default recorded at the wave 0 review.
why: Architecture v5 slide 11 requires an Idempotency-Key on every POST and a stored response per key, and names neither the header format, nor the scope tuple, nor the expiry window; the contract cannot be published without a read, and the scope must not be guessed per service.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (Idempotency-Key on every POST; Duplicates, order: a stored response); Ownership Map v1; RWB-PLT-TE006-CON section 12.7 (idempotency_key with the unique key on scope and key)
confirm: Platform team at the wave 0 review and the API review at the contract freeze
impact: Fixes the header name, the scope tuple and the expiry rule; the header format and the default window stay open until the review
